comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Impairment and Depreciation Charges Impacting Gross Margin
comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze the drivers of gross margin changes, but result in opposite outcomes. Broadcom's gross margin percentage decreased to 63% from 69% in 2024, primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix. Intel's consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion (20%) in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by substantial non-cash charges: $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation of manufacturing assets exceeding capacity and $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges. While Broadcom's margin decline is linked to software acquisition amortization and hardware mix, Intel's decline is linked to manufacturing asset impairments and inventory write-downs.

Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.

Broadcom reports that its 2024 gross margin percentage decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets and less favorable semiconductor product mix. Micron reports that its 2024 gross margin improved to 22% from -9% in 2023, primarily due to increases in average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, partially offset by the effects of inventory write-downs in 2023. While Broadcom's 2024 margin is compressed by amortization and mix, Micron's 2024 margin is recovering from prior-year inventory charges, illustrating different inventory and cost dynamics in the memory vs. mixed-signal/software semiconductor sectors.

comparisons.peer_topic: Gross Margin Year-over-Year Change and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023, primarily driven by 217% Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose a significant increase in gross margin percentage for fiscal year 2024 compared to the prior year. Broadcom increased to 63% from 69% (a decrease), whereas NVIDIA increased to 72.7% from 56.9%. Both attributions differ: Broadcom's change was negatively impacted by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangibles from the VMware merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix. In contrast, NVIDIA's margin expansion was driven by strong Data Center revenue growth (217%) and lower net inventory provisions. The comparison highlights divergent margin trajectories in the same fiscal year, with NVIDIA achieving high single-digit margin expansion while Broadcom faced margin compression due to acquisition accounting and mix.
